question: Assume today is 2026-09-05. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of new passenger cars (Pkw) registered in Germany in September 2026, as it will be first reported in the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt's (KBA) monthly press release on vehicle registrations.

target.what: Number of new passenger cars (Pkw) with first-time registration in Germany during September 2026, as reported by the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt (KBA) in its monthly press release on vehicle registrations (Fahrzeugzulassungen). Counts new Pkw only (Neuzulassungen von Personenkraftwagen), excluding used-car
target.cadence: monthly press release, typically published in the first days of the following month
target.caveats: Target period is future relative to the 2026-09-05 cutoff, so no September 2026 data exist yet; estimate must be built from prior-year seasonality, year-to-date 2026 momentum, order books, and calendar effects. Working interpretation: calendar-month total for September 2026 as first published (subje

candidates.hypothesis: September new Pkw registrations follow a recurring seasonal pattern (September is typically a strong month due to model-year/plate effects and Q3 push). Prior Septembers (2019, 2023, 2024, 2025) and the 2026 monthly run-rate anchor the level; September/adjacent-month ratio transfers the current level to September.
candidates.data_to_find: KBA monthly new Pkw registrations for September in 2019, 2023, 2024, 2025 and monthly values Jan–Aug 2026 (or latest available before cutoff); also September-to-August and September-to-annual ratios. Substitute: ACEA or VDA monthly Germany figures if KBA detail unavailable.

candidates.hypothesis: Germany is a stable share (~20–25%) of EU new car registrations; EU-wide September 2026 registrations (ACEA) times Germany's historical share gives an independent cross-check. Direction: if EU momentum is up, Germany likely up.
candidates.data_to_find: ACEA monthly new passenger car registrations for EU and Germany, Jan–Aug 2026 and September prior years; Germany share of EU total. Substitute: national association (VDA) or country-level data.

ACEA Germany passenger car registrations monthly 2026

candidates.hypothesis: Published 2026 forecasts (VDA, ifo, CAR-Center, Bloomberg/Reuters consensus) for German new car registrations and order intake imply a September level; order backlog and BEV incentive changes shift timing. Direction: higher order intake → higher September registrations with a lag.
candidates.data_to_find: 2026 full-year German new Pkw registration forecasts, monthly order intake (Auftragseingang) for German OEMs, and any September 2026 outlook published before cutoff. Substitute: ifo automotive business climate and VDA statements.

candidates.hypothesis: Policy changes (BEV purchase incentives, company-car tax rules, CO2/fleet rules) and macro conditions (interest rates, consumer confidence) can shift September registrations, especially pull-forward/pull-back around effective dates. Direction depends on timing of any incentive change.
candidates.data_to_find: Any German BEV/Pkw incentive or tax change effective around Q3/Q4 2026, plus consumer confidence and auto loan rate trends through Aug 2026. Substitute: news of registration pull-forward in Aug/Sep 2026.

candidates.hypothesis: Domestic registrations are supplied by domestic production plus imports minus exports; German Pkw production and export volumes (VDA/Statistisches Bundesamt) constrain the pool available for domestic registration. Direction: higher production/imports → higher potential registrations, with inventory buffer.
candidates.data_to_find: German Pkw production and exports (VDA/Statistik) for 2026 months, import volumes, and dealer inventory levels. Substitute: OEM Germany plant output reports.

candidates.hypothesis: September has a specific working-day count and seasonal multiplier relative to the annual run-rate; applying the 2026 YTD run-rate times a September seasonal factor yields the estimate. Direction: more working days / typical September strength → above-average month.
candidates.data_to_find: Working-day counts for September 2026 vs prior Septembers, and historical September seasonal factors (September registrations / average monthly registrations) for 2015–2025. Substitute: Eurostat or KBA calendar-adjusted series.

methods.label: m1

p56.role: August 2026 new Pkw registrations in Germany (KBA/VDA level)

a1.role: September/August seasonal multiplier for German new Pkw registrations

methods.rationale: Transfers the observed August 2026 level to September using a seasonal multiplier. Direct and uses the most recent kept level; main risk is that the September/August ratio is unstable across years (p2 vs p14).

methods.label: m2

p1.role: September 2025 new Pkw registrations in Germany (KBA level)

a2.role: year-on-year change factor for September 2026 vs September 2025

methods.rationale: Anchors on the same calendar month last year and applies the 2026 growth trend. Shares the a2 assumption with the 2026 momentum evidence; failure mode is a policy-driven break in the trend.

methods.label: m3
methods.rationale: Simple average of the two most recent kept September levels (2025 and 2023) as a low-information baseline; ignores 2026 momentum, so it is a conservative cross-check.

kept.name: September/August seasonal multiplier for German new Pkw registrations
kept.rationale: September 2025 was +13.7% vs August 2025 (p2), but September 2023 was -17.9% vs August 2023 (p14), and September production is far above August (p63 vs p71). The median of these signals is a modest uplift; the wide range reflects the observed instability of the September/August ratio.
kept.applies_when: August 2026 is a representative base month and no policy pull-forward distorts September 2026.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence of a September 2026 policy change or a very weak/strong early-September registration signal.

kept.name: Year-on-year change factor for September 2026 vs September 2025
kept.rationale: 2026 German registrations are running +5% YTD (p44, p33) with strong BEV momentum (+75% in August, p108) and order intake +64% YTD (p117); a modest continuation of the 2026 growth trend is assumed, with a wide range to cover policy and macro risk.
kept.applies_when: The 2026 growth trend persists into September without a major incentive change.
kept.falsified_by: A sharp reversal in BEV orders or a new purchase-tax/incentive change effective in September 2026.

Only the observed points are data; the multipliers are analyst assumptions. The main risk is an unstable September/August ratio or a policy-driven trend break. Better evidence would be actual September order books and daily registration data.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
